# CG-REQ-006: Request parameter removed

A documented parameter no longer exists.

**Why it matters:** Removal is usually tolerated on the wire (A6), but the consequence is a policy decision.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Requests](./#req) |
| Detects | `parameter.removed` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | yes |

## Message

> {where} was removed.
>
> Servers usually ignore unknown parameters, so requests still succeed, but any behaviour the parameter controlled is lost.
>
> **Fix:** Confirm that consumers do not rely on the behaviour the parameter controlled.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: filter removed (default policy)

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: q, in: query, schema: {type: string}}, {name: filter, in: query, schema: {type: string}}]
+       parameters: [{name: q, in: query, schema: {type: string}}]
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Non-breaking, info. GET /x: query parameter "filter" was removed.

### Fires: removedRequestParameters: potentially-breaking

With options: `{"policy":{"strictResponseValidation":false,"constraintTightening":"potentially-breaking","responseEnumAdditions":"potentially-breaking","removedRequestParameters":"potentially-breaking","closedResponseAdditions":"potentially-breaking"}}`

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: filter, in: query, schema: {type: string}}]
+       parameters: []
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, medium. GET /x: query parameter "filter" was removed.

### Does not fire: moved location

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: api_key, in: query, schema: {type: string}}]
+       parameters: [{name: api_key, in: header, schema: {type: string}}]
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- Servers that reject unknown parameters cannot be described in OpenAPI.
